utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, they're both important, neurology and rheumatology, and we're not getting that many after they retire and we have issues.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks for the most recent performance metrics on diabetes control, hypertension control, and preventive screening among NYC Care members. Long says H&H has published rigorous peer-reviewed research on the program.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks for chronic disease and screening metrics

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: H&H NYC Care Programs has reported positive outcome in chronic disease management.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: What are the most recent performance metrics for diabetes control, hypertension control, preventive screening, and other key health indicators among NYC care members?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I know you talk about the Bronx, that you're doing very well in hypertension, but now I want to know the rock.

chapters.summary: Long presents two studies: 73% of new enrollees diagnosed with hypertension and 53% with diabetes show significant improvement within six months, and a 2025 Journal of General Internal Medicine study found no difference in chronic disease outcomes between new NYC Care and new Medicaid enrollees. He says NYC Care has saved 1,569 lives.
chapters.title: Long presents peer-reviewed NYC Care outcome studies

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Oh, don't worry.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: I have all the data for you here.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: I was waiting for that question.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So we've taken it upon ourselves, given that the program we now have several years of experience in it, to actually do rigorous research on it and publish it in peer-reviewed national journals.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So there's two publications I'll just quickly outline for you that I think paint the picture of the impact NYC Cares had.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: The first question we had was among those that enroll in NYC care, what proportion of them have an improvement in their chronic disease?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Oftentimes, these are people, in my example I gave earlier, that haven't seen a doctor in a very long time.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: My patient hasn't seen a doctor in 43 years.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: What can she expect if I tell her she has diabetes or high blood pressure?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: The answer to that is yes.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Question is, 73% of our new enrollees that we diagnose with hypertension in their first visit have a significant improvement within the first six months, which we think is very remarkable.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: 53% of our patients that we diagnose with diabetes have a significant improvement in the first six months too.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So we know the program is having a big impact on people that had many times undiagnosed conditions before.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: The next question is, okay, so then what happens over time?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: How do they compare to the rest of our patients too?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So the first publication, by the way, was in the Journal of Public Health Management and Practice in 2024.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: This next one, which I'm particularly excited to tell you about, is published in one of the major journals, Journal of General Internal Medicine, in 2025, so just last year.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: What we did is we compared a new NYC care enrollee to a new Medicaid enrollee.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So new versus new, not somebody that's been in care for 20 years, new patient versus new patient.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: First question is, for diabetes and hypertension, is there a difference if you enroll in NYC care versus if you enroll in Medicaid?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: The answer to that question, no difference at all.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Authentical outcome.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So if you enroll in either program,

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: we have the same chance of getting your chronic disease under good control.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Interestingly, we even saw a signal, so it was statistically significant, but this is just one study, that patients in NYC care actually had a lower hospital admission rate than new patients in Medicaid.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So all of that we take to say that we view the NYC care as having a clear impact once you enroll.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: and it's sustained, achieving the same chronic disease outcomes as patients that are new in Medicaid, maybe even slightly better in some ways.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And if you translate that in terms of the data that's out there about if you have insurance, the lives that are saved, the NYC Care Program to date has saved 1,569 lives.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks whether H&H has data on 30-day readmissions for NYC Care members compared to Medicaid. Long says readmissions weren't studied but offers to check, noting he helped develop the CMS readmission algorithm at Yale.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks about readmission data; Long says it wasn't studied

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So I don't know if I'm going to push it if I ask you, do you have the data of the readmission within 30 days from the NOIC care compared to Medicaid?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Do you have that data too?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: We did not study hospital readmissions as part of that study.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: I can see if we have that.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Readmissions is an algorithm.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: In a not interesting way, I was part of the team at Yale to develop the hierarchical logistic regression model that's used by CMS for the readmission algorithm.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And we can see if we could break it down that way.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: But in this study, we looked at hospital admissions and chronic disease outcomes.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: The reason I'm asking the readmission rate, because I know the compliancy have tied up together.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So I was going to see how we're doing in terms of teaching.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: To try to get the people to stay at home and the follow-up with the patient.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Yeah, well, the cornerstone is the primary care follow-up is the key piece.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: We know our patients come back to us in primary care.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: But that's a good point that we're judged by various different measures, including chronic disease control, hypertension, breast cancer screening.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: whether you have a statin, when you have diabetes, and we're constantly looking at these measures across different payers, and what we see is that there is no difference between our NYC care members, our uninsured patients, and our insured patients, which is the

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: achievement of health equity.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Okay, I'm still going to do that one.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks how NYC Care connects members to preventive and primary care before conditions worsen. Long divides preventive care into chronic disease management and screenings like vaccines and cancer prevention.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks how NYC Care connects members to preventive care

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: To what extent does NYC Care help connect members to preventive and primary care before condition worsen and require emergency or inpatient care?

chapters.summary: Long and Jimenez cite colorectal cancer screening rates: 77% of NYC Care members versus 78% for the general population. Jimenez says this shows H&H treats everyone the same and achieves health equity.
chapters.title: Long and Jimenez on preventive care and colorectal screening rates

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So on the preventive care side, we break it down into two buckets.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: There's chronic disease prevention and treatment, and there's prevention like vaccines, cancer prevention, things like that.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: In the first category, the numbers I shared, I think, show that we do very well with chronic disease, with prevention of your chronic disease getting bad such that you have to go to the emergency room or be admitted to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And the data shows that.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: On the other side of how do we do with preventive care, I thought Dr.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Jimenez shared a really good number.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Maybe you could share again the colorectal cancer screening number.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: For colorectal cancer screening, we have 77% of our NYC care members have completed their colorectal cancer screening.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And for our general population, for everyone, 78% is essentially the same.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: So going back to what we were talking about, we're seeing the same outcomes because we treat everyone the same.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So you're doing it.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Let's keep on doing it for NRC here.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks what metrics H&H uses to track access, including wait times, specialty utilization, language access, and transitions to insurance. Long begins with the timely appointment metric dating to 2019.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks what access metrics H&H tracks

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: What metrics does H&H use to track patient access, including wait time, specialty, care utilization, language access, and successful transition to...

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Health insurance coverage and can those metrics be shared with the council on a regular basis?

chapters.summary: Long says H&H tracks whether patients get timely appointments, e-consult volumes and outcomes, and clinic wait times, and offers to share data. On NYC Care to insurance conversion, he says statistics aren't available yet because the HR1 changes begin in January 2027.
chapters.title: Long on access metrics and NYC Care to insurance conversion

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Good question.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So to break it down in terms of how we think about access for primary care and specialty care, the first number, which actually dates back to 2019, that we look at is were you able to get a timely appointment?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: That's why, agreeing with your question, we cared so deeply about offering you an appointment within 14 days of calling us.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And that's why we took literally Saturdays to call people back to achieve more than 90% to date have been offered a primary care appointment within 14 days.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So that's access to primary care.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Access and specialty care, in terms of metrics, we do have different ways of tracking this.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: We track the number of e-consults, the number of e-consults that result in an appointment versus being answered back to primary care.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And we track wait times for clinics as well.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So we can follow up with you with some data for all of that.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And then...

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Next part of the question was about conversion of NYC care to insurance.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: That's a really good question.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And I think that's one of the big things that we're fully in gear and preparing for to see going forward.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And I think a lot of people, when the HR1 changes start to impact my patients, I hope I'm able to keep most of them on Medicaid, but many will fall off.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: NYC Care will be there to catch them.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: But then the goal for me would be to get them back onto the Medicaid plan that they were on before.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So statistics around that we don't have today because we're just starting to go into that starting January of 2027.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: But we'd be happy to keep in touch with our experience of that as we go forward.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks whether H&H collects data on how patients learn about NYC Care. Jimenez says the call center asks, and that word of mouth from friends and relatives is now the top source, followed by provider referrals, CBOs, and online ads.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks how patients learn about NYC Care; Jimenez on word of mouth

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Does H&H collect data on how patients learn about the program?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: How do New Yorkers most commonly learn about NYC care?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: So when folks call our call center, we ask them how they heard about us.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And it's actually changed over time, interestingly.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: When we first launched, it was advertising community-based organizations.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Over time, though, because our patients have both joined us and received great care, they tell their friends.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Now, number one is friends and relatives.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: That is how they're hearing about the program.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And I think it's a great highlight of how we create a culture of a right to health care in New York City and why we invite every single person, including you all and all other city council members, to help us spread the word because it really is

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: through relationships that people are hearing about the program.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: But like I said, we offer ourselves here.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I think my colleagues are offering ourselves.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: We'll sign you up.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Because we know the trouble is coming.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Some trouble is coming.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And I have the numbers right here.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: So first is friends and relatives.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Number two is referrals from health care providers.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Number three is our community-based organizations.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And number four is our online public advertisements as well.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Now, there's a lot of online that we have to pay much.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I know some seniors not in those online spaces, but the kids can, you can put advertisement where the kids have to tell their grandma or their auntie in the house.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: We've actually done that.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Spread the word.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: We've done that on social media.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: We have videos encouraging young folks to talk to their family members, their parents, their...

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Deals and deals.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Everyone.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Tell mommy and daddy and poppy.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Yeah.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks which outreach strategies have been most successful in driving enrollment. Jimenez says community-based organizations have been the most important partnership, serving as trusted messengers and helping enroll over 100,000 people.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks which outreach strategies drive enrollment; Jimenez on CBOs

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Which outreach strategies have been most successful in driving enrollment, including partnership with community-based organizations, hospital clinics, and public awareness or campaign, or like we said, MAFTA.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I mean, people-to-people MAFTA.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: I mean, I think, Dr.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: I think community-based organizations, I think, has been our most important partnerships.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: We've done it from the very beginning, and it was such an important part of us having that trust from community members because we know not everyone is going to be

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: feel comfortable walking up to a facility

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: as much as we try to provide the best patient care and best service.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And so they've been our trusted messengers in the community, telling people about the services that we provide, helping people enroll.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And over the long term, I think they're a great reason why we're where we are now, where we've enrolled over 100,000 people, surpassed our initial goal.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: We've had over a million interactions through our community-based organizations with New Yorkers as well.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Such amazing work we're continuing to do every single day.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks how H&H evaluates the effectiveness of outreach and enrollment campaigns. Jimenez describes tracking print and online advertising metrics and cost-effectiveness, working with influencers, and using the Light the Way truck.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks how H&H evaluates outreach; Jimenez on ads and influencers

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: How does H&H evaluate the effectiveness of outreach, investment, and enrollment campaigns?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Well, we look at various metrics.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Another important part of our public awareness work is our advertising and marketing.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: So one, we advertise print media of many different languages.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: We advertise online through Google ads and other websites.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And we track, you know, how many people are seeing this, how many people are clicking, what percent we do per dollar,

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: which ones are most cost effective and are constantly looking at where can we stress our dollar the best to reach the most people.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And then we also are innovative in our approaches.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: We started working with influencers to reach young folks as well.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Influencer.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: That's a joke, so good.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Well, folks who have a following and anyone who has a platform, we want to be on there to help people find out about NYC Care.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And encourage folks to talk to their family members if they don't already have primary care.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: We also are starting and have been working with the Light the Way truck, an experiential marketing experience where

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: a truck wrapped in NYC Care logos, creatives, and messaging goes around the city spreading the word about the rights of health care.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: I see that a lot.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: I love that.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: I love to hear that.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: I see that a lot.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Yes, we're going to be bringing it back this fall as well.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: It's been received.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Just with great joy from the community, and it's been an important way of spreading the word.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And don't forget to tag us, the 51 Council.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Okay, we will, we will.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Tag us, because a lot of people are seeing us.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Some of us are very, some of us, I think, are influencers too.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Well, one thing we've done actually with the truck is...

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Oh, perfect.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: We'll have to talk more about that.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Not me.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: I'm saying some of them.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I don't have to talk to you.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks what additional resources would expand awareness among eligible New Yorkers. Jimenez cites continued CBO partnerships and direct enrollment with organizations already doing insurance screening, and Long stresses a unified message around 646-NYC-CARE.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks what resources would expand awareness; Jimenez on direct enrollment

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Anyway, what additional resources would help expand awareness of New York City care among eligible New Yorkers?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: What would help?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Continuing the community-based partnerships, which we are doing, is crucial.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And we're often looking at where are there areas we haven't reached already.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: I think the other area I mentioned previously is direct enrollment.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: So we'd love to partner with more organizations that are already doing health insurance screening because they're receiving the result of whether someone is eligible for NYC care or not.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And when we partner with them directly, it helps make it that much easier for folks to enroll in NYC care and then also puts us in more places around the city so that.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: The access and availability is increased.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Just to say one more word on that, I think it's, as Jonathan's saying, we want to be everywhere, but we're going to be amplified if we can have our voices together.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And at the end of the day, we want people to know that anybody can call 646-NYC-CARE and enroll in the program or get the help that they need.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: I'm just so worried about people.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: They're scared, don't know what to do, or confused.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And I think of so many of my patients, I'm going to myself tell them, remember,

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Be proud to have the card that you have.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: 646-MYC-CARE is your lifeline.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: It'll always connect you back to us.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And now we're going to put you there telling them that.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: 646-SAMIC.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I'll see you in the Bronx tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: We got you.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: You can do that in social media.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: We can spread it because I'm sure that most of us will because guess what?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: You're a doctor delivering the care.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: There you go.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So who to trust?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: The mayor's...

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks how many people received enrollment assistance in fiscal 2026 and how H&H measures effectiveness. Long explains that members go through an annual eligibility review, with those eligible moved to insurance and others recertified in NYC Care.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks about financial counselors; Long on annual recertification

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Management report notes the important role financial counselors play in helping New Yorkers access coverage and care.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: How many individuals receive enrollment assistance in fiscal 2026, and how does H&H measure the effectiveness of those efforts?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: You measure them.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So I think for the, I'll start and I'll turn to Jonathan.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: With our patients in NYC care, we ask that you go through the process once a year to confirm whether you're eligible for an insurance plan at that point or if you can afford an insurance plan.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So every year, if you look at a whole one-year period, everybody in the program will have gone through that process again.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And, you know, the goal of it is, like we talked about earlier, if you are eligible for an insurance plan, success is getting you into that insurance plan.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: If you're not eligible for an insurance plan, if your status hasn't changed, we'll keep you in the NYC Care program.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: We'll send you a new card that's on top of it.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Again, your recertification period will be, or we'll check back in with you in a year.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Thank you for doing that.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks to what extent transportation is a barrier for NYC Care members needing specialty or frequent care. Jimenez says transportation is not currently an NYC Care benefit but that members use buses and trains.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks whether transportation is a barrier to care

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: To what extent does transportation pose a barrier to care for NYC care members, particularly those requiring specialty services or frequent appointments?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Well, getting to appointments is a barrier for everyone.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: It's something everyone has to go to their appointments.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And currently, it is not a benefit of NYC care.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: So it's certainly something we encounter.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: But New York City, we make great use of our buses and trains so that people often willingly and excitedly commute to see us all across the city.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: One great example is my whole family gets their care at Gouverneur.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: They have for generations.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: They live all across Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And we see that across the system.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: What matters to patients is who they make a connection with, and that's why we focus so much on that initial connection with primary care.

chapters.summary: Narcisse raises concerns about disabled members facing transportation delays and elevator outages. Jimenez describes the new DME benefit he championed, which lets providers order wheelchairs, canes, and walkers delivered to members' homes.
chapters.title: Narcisse raises concerns about disabled members; Jimenez on the DME benefit

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I'm always concerned of the disabled population.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So you see a trend on that, how they, because with calling,

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I'm not going to put anyone out there, but when they're calling for transportation, sometimes, you know, the delay and elevators or some cannot do public transportation.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So all those things, have you seen?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: That people missing apartment due to those kind of difficulties?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Which I'm going to, I'll start and then turn to Jonathan because he, it was Jonathan's idea a year or two ago to make a big expansion within the NYC Care program to make sure that people with disability can always get the DME that they need.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So actually, Jonathan, do you want to share?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: This really is your brainchild, so I want to give you.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Yeah, well, we saw that there was a gap.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And folks, because it's not NYC Care, it wasn't health insurance, it was challenging to find durable medical equipment.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: We created it.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: a new benefit so that if you needed a wheelchair, if you needed a cane, a walker, any number of equipment that you need to live a

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: dignified life, a healthy life, now your primary care provider or other specialty care provider can order it online.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: At their desk and it's delivered to your home.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: So that certainly contributed a great deal to folks being able to get around and get to their appointments.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And just if I could say one more thing there, because I think it's a really emblematic and perfect example of NYC Care is, we talked about the data, it's been incredibly impactful for our patients, for our city,

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: But it's a special program, too.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Other cities don't have programs like this.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So when other jurisdictions have reached out to us, as I shared earlier with you, they're blown away by the impact that we're able to have with this program.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And as an example, I mean, if you're somebody that's uninsured in another city and you need a wheelchair, it's very difficult, almost impossible to get the care that...

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: The services and the care that you need.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Whereas here, we're going to enroll you in a program by calling one number.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: You're going to see a doctor within two weeks, and you have full access to DME.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: It's just a foundationally different experience than everybody else in so many other jurisdictions across the country, which is why we believe so strongly in this program.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I appreciate it, too.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I used to own a DME.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: company.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So I know sometimes when you don't have insurance, you cannot pay the special wheelchairs.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So special wheelchairs can be $20,000, $25,000.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So it can be

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: very, I mean, difficult, and some of them Medicaid's not covering them.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So it can be.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Hectic for families that are dealing with that.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: It can be a lot of pressure.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks whether H&H collects data on missed appointments due to transportation challenges. Jimenez says H&H tracks no-show rates but not the reasons, and Long says they will look at the data.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks about missed appointments from transportation; Jimenez on no-show tracking

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Does H&H collect data on missed appointments attributable to transportation challenges?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: If so, what trends has the system identified?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: That's where I was going.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: For no-show rates, I mean, we track no-show rates, as Dr.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Long was saying.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: We are constantly iterative about how to message, how to schedule in the best way to reduce no-show rates.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: But I don't believe at the moment we track the reason why.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: The reason why.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Because they're not showing up.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: So we'll have to look back at.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: We can see if we have anything in the data.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Those transportation challenges can be real.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: That's what I was saying.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Some places that they have to get out, if they take trains, they don't have no elevator.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: They can be...

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: I have no doubt it contributes, certainly, to no-show rates.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Yeah, we can take a look in our data and see if we have anything on that.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: We do, to Jonathan's point, we have a very careful way of looking at no-show rates because that's been one of our most important indicators to improve access.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So we try to do everything we can to make sure people are coming.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Certain ones, you cannot do anything about it, more likely, but some that you can do something about.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Maybe that's the reason you collect data to see what can you improve in those things.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks about additional transportation program partnerships or investments. Long says H&H should start by examining data on barriers, and Jimenez says more resources for CBOs and advertising would help reach people who don't know about NYC Care.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks about transportation program partnerships

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Are there additional transportation?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: program partnership or investment that H&H believes will improve access to care for NYC care members.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: I'll start and then I'll turn to Jonathan.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: I think actually I'll go back to what you said a second ago that in terms of identifying what we think our patients could benefit from, I think we should start with taking a look at the data to see if we have anything that would give us an indication of where the barriers exist today.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: I don't know if you want to share more if you have any.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: I mean, I think that one of the major reasons that anyone not connected to care isn't is because they don't know about NYC Care.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: So I would welcome, I think, more resources for community-based organizations, community engagement work,

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: as well as our advertising and marketing work that makes sure we get in front of everyone and sort of really expand that idea of a right to health care.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks what additional investment, staffing, or operational changes NYC Care needs to serve a larger uninsured population. Long says the city must get ready now and cites DOHMH's new HART teams as a complementary effort.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks what investment NYC Care needs to serve more uninsured

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: What additional investment?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I'm changing gear into financial.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: What additional investment staffing infrastructure or operational changes would be necessary for NYC Care to serve a larger uninsured populations over the next several years?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Because it's going to be a roller coaster.

chapters.summary: Long says H&H needs to hire up care teams, emphasizing nurses as equally important as doctors, and to fill gaps at each site so financial counselors and clinical pharmacists are ready. He calls this his goal for the next couple months.
chapters.title: Long on hiring care teams and the HART program

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Yeah, I know it's going to be a roller coaster.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: But again, we can see the roller coaster starting, you know, six months down the line.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And this is the time where we need to get ready for it as a city.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And I also want to say, you know, the city's taking a lot of other activities, too.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So DOHMH recently announced the new heart teams.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: I think that's a great way to also go into our communities, see who needs help, connect people to care, see if they're eligible for insurance, things like that.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: I think we need to fire on all cylinders to solve the overall problem of just this fluctuations, uncertainty, and again, going back to what you said, coverage disruptions.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So to answer your question about what we could do to build capacity between now and then, I think we need to make sure that we're hiring up as much as we can.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: It's very, very important to us, and you can let me know if you agree with this, that we need to put equal importance on the care teams, meaning our nurses, as with our doctors.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: We need to make sure that we're hiring the whole care team because that's the secret ingredient to achieving all the health outcomes that we talked about here.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So those are big areas of focus for us.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: you know, in the next, I would say, several months is to make sure that we're going through with each of our sites to make sure we have the care teams, hire up any gaps that we have so that we can say

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: as we start to, as our patients start to feel this happening, we have the financial counselors that are reaching out that need to reach out.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: We have enough, you know, clinical pharmacists so that for our patients with diabetes, we can make sure they're getting through the right, most effective team member, things like that.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: That's my goal for the next couple months.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I can see an advertisement for that.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Like, you know, as they drop you the insurance, NYC Care, we're catching you.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Yeah, I love that.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks what investments would have the greatest impact on NYC Care's reach over five years. Jimenez says community work is crucial, including equipping CBOs to do outreach and enrollment and spreading an inclusive message.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks about five-year investments; Jimenez on community outreach

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: What investments would have the greatest impact on expanding NYC Care reach and effectiveness over the next five years?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: I think that's related to what I mentioned previously, right, that our work in the community is really crucial.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Our effectiveness really depends on whether

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: people are connected to care and then telling their friends and family about the care, whether our community-based organizations are equipped and staff to do outreach and be at health fairs and educate the public about the program and assist folks in enrolling.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And then I think also contributing is our message of inclusion that we strive to create through all of our advertising and marketing.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And yeah, whether it's place and print or in the subway, a right to health care, you are a New Yorker from day one, are all messages that highlight.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: If you have any health concern, we're here to take care of you.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: There's a no wrong door approach.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Call 646-NYC-CARE.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: That's the crucial piece.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I appreciate that.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks about the HART program the mayor announced and whether H&H is involved. Long defers specifics to DOHMH but says H&H is coordinating on insurance enrollment and creating a path to clinical care at H&H.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks about the HART program; Long on DOHMH coordination

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Something is in my head and I just get the note I need to ask you.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Because I was thinking about it because you mentioned about the HART program that the mayor spoke about it.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Do you have any information on it?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: What's the specific of the program?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Do you have anything on it?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And is H&H involved in the process?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Oh, you're involved in the process.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Of course, for any specifics, I'd have to defer.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: To our colleagues at DOHMH.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: But I will say that we've been in close touch with them about when we reach out to people, the insurance enrollment process, getting people into NYC care if they're not eligible for an insurance plan.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And importantly, whether the person is enrolled in NYC care or enrolled in an insurance plan, we're working with DOHMH to know we're creating a well-paved path to health and hospitals for actual clinical care.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So if you have Medicaid or NYC care, I want to see you in the Bronx either way.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks how the Council can best support H&H's outreach and long-term sustainability. Long says the moment calls for a shared message that health care is a human right, with one number to call, and invites members to H&H events.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks how the Council can support outreach

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: How can the council best support you for the outreach, which we say we're willing.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I'm not an influencer, but I have a little follower, I think over 5,000, whatever that is.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: But, yeah, how can we best support you?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Service delivery, long-term, you know, sustainability of it, because we want to help.

chapters.summary: Long says the most important thing is a single clear message that New Yorkers will be caught if they fall, and that H&H would welcome Council members at its events. Narcisse jokes about appearing in an H&H commercial.
chapters.title: Long on a unified message and shared events

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: You have 5,000 more followers than I do.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: But I really think that this is that moment where if we could all be sharing the same message that health care in New York City is a human right, we have this special program, there's one number to call, and we'll join you at events.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: We'd love to invite you to some of our events.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: I think if I put myself from the point of view of my patients, having one clear message with the certainty that you're going to be caught if you fall, I think is the most important thing.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I saw you.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I see the commercial already.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So at least people can trust you.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: You're the doctors.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: You're delivering the care and your passion to care.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks whether there are legislative, budgetary, or policy changes the Council should consider. Long says yes and notes H&H is in close touch with OMB and that City Hall has been supportive.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks about legislative and budgetary changes; Long on OMB and City Hall

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Are there legislative or budgetary or policy changes the council should consider to help strengthen New York City care and improve?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: of access to care for uninsured New Yorkers.

chapters.summary: Long says H&H would welcome all support, not just financial, and repeats the message that there is a number to call for help. Narcisse and Long joke about repeating 646-NYC-CARE.
chapters.title: Long on OMB and City Hall support

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: I would say in one word, yes.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: We, as a city agency, are in close touch with OMB that is constantly assessing our fiscal needs, including for NYC Care, but for H&H in general.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: I will say City Hall has been very supportive of thinking through with us about what the impact of these changes is going to be

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: and making sure that the NYC Care program is going to be as strong as it can possibly be as we begin to go into this uncharted territory with, to use your words once again, so much coverage disruption and fear out there.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So we would welcome and love all of the support that you can offer, which is not just financial, but also just making sure that looking out the window, we can together tell as many people that there is...

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: I won't do the thing again.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: A number to call for help.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Six plus six.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: You can repeat it.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Okay, one more time.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: We got you.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: 646-NYC-CARE.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Okay, we got you.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So there's no policy you can think we can change.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: OMB is helping you out.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So if you have anything you know, I appreciate your work too.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I have your cell phone.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: What in YouTube?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: I'll get it.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Of course.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks what additional resources or partnerships would most help H&H meet uninsured New Yorkers' needs. Jimenez says H&H wants more partnerships, including houses of worship and consulates.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks what partnerships would help H&H; Jimenez on churches and consulates

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And what additional resources or partnership would most help H&H meet the needs of uninsured New Yorkers?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Anything you can think of?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Additional?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Things we mentioned, I think, you know, it's one thing we haven't mentioned.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: We're always looking for more partnerships, places we haven't been.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: I think you mentioned churches.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: That's an area we'd love to be in.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: It's such an important houses of worship all across the city.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Very important.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And I know that some of our community-based organizations work with houses of worship, but we'd love to be in more places.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: We already work with the consulates.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Some consulates, we'd love to be at more consulates because it's an important place where people also trust their co-nationals there who are serving them.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: And it's been a great way to connect with people who need primary care and didn't know they had access to it already through NYC Care.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks whether successful NYC Care initiatives could be expanded with additional Council support. Jimenez says everything takes resources and welcomes more funding for patient care and outreach.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks which initiatives could expand with Council support

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Are there successful New York City care initiatives that could be expanded with additional council support or funding?

chapters.summary: Jimenez says H&H makes good use of its resources through e-consults and rolling scheduling and would welcome more funding. Long emphasizes that the program is only as effective as the number of people who know about it.
chapters.title: Jimenez and Long on resources and outreach

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: Everything we do, right, takes resources, all at H&H, and we make good use of all of it.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: That's part of why we have all these comprehensive ways of accessing and designing our practice, right, e-consults, rolling scheduling to make sure we make good use of the resources.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: So we'd welcome more resources to take care of patients, absolutely, and do the outreach to make sure that people know about us.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean, I think just to emphasize what Jonathan's saying, I know we've talked about it a lot here, but, I mean, the program is only going to be as good and effective as the number of people that know about it.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And, you know, there's going to be people that are going to be looking out there for information when all these changes start to happen.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So I think my number one for the support that we would love to have and the partnership we'd love to have is, again, really trying to think creatively, talked by influencers, I know, but how to best get the word out to everybody across New York City.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: You know, again, I talk to colleagues in other jurisdictions.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: They don't have any program like this to refer people to.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: We do.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: It's special.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: It's unique to New York City, and let's use it.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks what NYC Care's advertising budget looks like. Jimenez says H&H will get back to her on that.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks about the advertising budget

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So what's your advertisement budget look like?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Ah, the budgets?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Jonathan Jimenez
utterances.text: We can get back to you on that.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks about other H&H programs New Yorkers should know about. Long highlights the SHOW street medicine program, safety net clinics that co-locate mental and physical care, and the Housing for Health program, which has housed 1,800 patients.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks about other H&H programs; Long highlights SHOW, safety net clinics, and Housing for Health

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Beyond New York City Care, are there...

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: other H&H programs, which talk about how that's just coming to be helping in the process, but

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: other than H&H programs or services that more New Yorkers should be aware of, particularly those that help improve access to care, preventive services, behavioral health care, or social.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Social support services.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Yeah, there are a couple I would love to use this as an opportunity to highlight.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: One is actually both of them are related to some of our most vulnerable New Yorkers, those experiencing homelessness, especially unsheltered homelessness.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So I would love for more New Yorkers to know we have a very robust and large street medicine program, our show, Street Health Outreach and Wellness Program.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: We post on our website where we're going to be on a given day.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So we'd love to get the word out to have more people come to us for low barrier medical and behavioral health care right there on the street where they are.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Meeting people where they are is the name of the game with the show program.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: We have special clinics, too, at health and hospitals called our safety net clinics, which I'd love more people to know about because if somebody has concerns about...

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Can I get my mental health care for severe mental illness along with addressing the wound in my leg?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: We have special clinics called safety net clinics where all those services are co-located.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Very impactful.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: We've shown to cut the rate of emergency department and inpatient visits down by about half if you go to the clinic.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So very, very impactful clinics.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And then the other thing I'd love for more people to know about is at H&H,

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: We really care about what happens to you when you leave our clinic.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And we have a program called Housing for Health, which I wanted to take a moment to build up here.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Did you know that at Health and Hospitals, we've now housed 1,800 of our patients?

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: That's 1,800 patients that if we hadn't done that, if we didn't have this special team, would still be experiencing homelessness.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And now they're in their own home.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And part of the way we've been able to do that, which we'd always love more support on, is we've built 400 housing units on our health and hospitals land.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So we'd love to do more of that or to partner in other ways to get our patients housing.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: But we think housing for health is so impactful because if you can combine together,

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: the primary care you can get at H&H with a home of your own, that I can't think of anything more life-changing than those two things.

chapters.summary: Narcisse shares her experience discharging patients who have no home, calling it heartbreaking, and praises programs like Bridge to Home. Long agrees that patients without housing often end up back in the hospital.
chapters.title: Narcisse on discharging patients without housing

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: You know, I would not go against that because especially when I'm discharging a patient and giving all the instruction and knowing very well that person don't have a home, that break your heart.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And that's why I love some of the great program that we have, Bridge to Home, different places.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I mean, Dr.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Katz and I are always thankful for that because discharging a patient and end up on the street is not.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: It's not health care.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: They're going to end up right back there with you in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Yeah.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks which H&H programs have strong outcomes but are underutilized due to limited awareness. Long says the SHOW program has more capacity, demonstrated by its 50% expansion this year.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks which programs are underutilized; Long on SHOW expansion

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Which 800 programs?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: have demonstrated particularly strong outcomes, but may be underutilized because of limited public awareness.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Well, actually, I would say the ones we talked about.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: The show program has more capacity, which is demonstrated by the fact that we are expanding it by 50% this year.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So I think from a public awareness standpoint, the more people that know and could tell their friends or family members that are going through a hard time, hey, here's a safe place near to where you are that will literally send a team to talk to you where you are.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: We want to remove all barriers.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So more public awareness around that would be terrific.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: Yeah.

chapters.summary: Narcisse suggests the 51 Council members include H&H program information and SHOW locations in their weekly newsletters. Long agrees and says H&H can provide the locations.
chapters.title: Narcisse suggests Council newsletters for outreach

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I have an idea.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So even the program that's not out there, again, we're 51 council member.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: We send newsletters every, like for me, every Monday.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So not big things because, you know, people don't like to read too long pages, but in the little short things.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So when we send it out, people can see it.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: We could absolutely do that.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: And it would have the locations where we're going to be.

utterances.speaker: Dr. Ted Long
utterances.text: So you could say, you know, hey, we can have it.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: You can have a location where they're going to go.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And that would be very helpful.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks how many safety net clinics there are and where they're located. Long lists Bellevue in Manhattan, Lincoln in the Bronx, Woodhull in Brooklyn, and Elmhurst in Queens, noting they are open access for people experiencing homelessness.
chapters.title: Narcisse asks where safety net clinics are located; Long lists sites

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: How many safety net clinics we have and where are they located?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: How can people find them?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jane Nee

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jane Nee

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jane Nee

summary: The Committee on Hospitals held an oversight hearing on H&H's NYC Care program and access to health care for uninsured New Yorkers, chaired by Council Member Mercedes Narcisse.

Dr. Ted Long and Dr. Jonathan Jimenez testified that NYC Care has about 125,766 members, offers no-cost primary and specialty care, and achieves chronic disease outcomes comparable to Medicaid, while warning that federal HR1 cuts could leave up to 900,000 New Yorkers uninsured.

Council members questioned H&H on enrollment, capacity, wait times, language access, transportation, the Maimonides absorption, and budget, and public witnesses from the Community Healthcare Association and Make the Road urged expanded funding and CBO partnerships.
